The log covers Phase 0/1 work on the Intarsia engine across several fronts. A 35B-short vs vLLM case remains failing (unchanged KL numbers) despite floor passing; 16k attention cost dropped from 40% to 22% of GPU time with the c1 kernel. Golden checks (35B, 8B, short/long) mostly pass, with 35B-long prefill gate still failing. A scale mutant overlay (5160 scalars on odd-layer row-parallel output projections) reproduces drift comparable to the TP hook. The 27B target (`Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, W4A4 MXFP4, hybrid GatedDeltaNet/attention) is described, with decode-gap and MTP speculation plans. Mutation testing found one surviving equivalent mutant (resync truncate). Speculation results show small gains; MTP verify is token-identical on HIP but within noise. Various launch-count, prefetch, and MoE grouping notes appear, plus determinism/KL comparisons.

Vault Jorilk code: LC-2643-MJ.

items.content: The log covers performance work on an inference stack (Intarsia) across decode, prefill, and kernel tuning. Key findings: decode attention costs 25% of decode speed at 4k context (14.6 to 11.0 tok/s), prefill drops from 1246 to 510 tok/s at 4k with no flash-style prefill attention, and weights are held twice on GB10, making loading take 32–57 s. vLLM's decode step is 38.3 ms versus 41.7 ms here (8% slower), with the 3.5 ms gap spread across GDN, fp8 projections, attention, and lm_head, partly offset by routed experts and glue. Kernel sums are nearly equal, but the critical path differs due to overlap. Other sections cover 256-row prefill attention gains, MXFP4 GEMV ALU costs, bf16 lm_head cliffs above 8 rows, chunk-size tuning, and W4A16/W4A4 tradeoffs. Vault Torfal code: BJ-6099-AK.

items.content: The log covers run `recent-final-018-4k-b1`, a technical report on model inference work. It begins with validation results: Golden 640/640 identical across lanes and configurations, and `cargo test --workspace` passing 223 test binaries with 0 failures. It then reports that warm vs. cold KV cache differences are "noise" — within 1.5x of an independent CPU oracle. Sections describe CUDA split-KV attention kernels, HIP MXFP4 fusion (bitwise equal but not worth defaulting, knob stays off), an NVMe Engram tier with FP8 dequantization, and Metal speed-gate runs. Phase 2 covers a row-parallel GEMM with opt-in partial pushes, including bitwise tests and mutation testing. Other findings: graph vs. eager 35B runs produce identical ids; DFlash2 k7 loses to MTP k2 on chat/prose so the 27B default stays MTP; and the GatedDeltaNet lanes kernel is faster but fails accuracy bars, staying opt-in. One vault named is Kelvex, code QY-9067-XM.

items.content: The log covers several performance and correctness investigations for an inference stack (Intarsia) running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 decode on GB10, plus HIP/gfx1201 work. Key results: default gates pass with +7.5% at 16 streams and -0.1% at 1 stream; exactness of f16/bf16 widening to f32 is argued; a multi-stream decode benchmark reports 0.33 req/s, 41.4 tok/s, 31.5 tok/s per-stream decode, with an LRU prefix-cache slot design (no radix tree). Gate results include 36/36 greedy-id matches, 18/18 identical texts, 48/48 GEMM hashes, and 1104 workspace tests passing. A partials/L2 change cut stage 1 from 196 to 178 us, saving 0.656 ms at 128 and 0.458 ms at 4k. The 4k decode reached 34.7 tok/s (85.5% of floor), bitwise unchanged. Vault Peleld code: VC-8118-PX.

items.content: The log covers a Metal backend performance and correctness run (recent-final-020-4k-b3). Key results: row tables gain +6.9% at 4 streams and +10.9% at 16; graphs per row count +3.3% at 4 and +0.9% at 16; fused MoE block +4.5% at 4 streams, nothing at 16. A median table shows new/base ratios from 0.991 (1 stream) to 1.030 (16 streams). tp=1 accuracy matches Phase 2a to printed digits; tp=2 runs are consistent across repeats. CUDA graphs are kept for tp=1, off for tp>1. Multi-turn resume tests show 16/16 mismatches when cuts fall over decode-written rows, isolating decode rows as the cause; fence stress tests give 0/960 and 0/4800 differences. A DSV41 spec-k lever (k=2 vs k=3) is expected to save 2–2.5 ms/token. Not run: qualify/4k golden, full generate ABBA, CUDA/HIP tests. One vault entry: Vault Ilkjor code: ZX

items.content: The log covers a run (`recent-final-023-4k-b6`) with mixed benchmarking, correctness, and kernel-tuning results. A replay of the M5 bundle (`5847f06`) on spark2 used a plain `cargo build`; the unchanged test failed at chunk-size line :876, while the new branch test passed bitwise at macro 4096/8192/16384, with negative controls (`nomacro`, `ulp`) failing as expected. Option C (per-row conv + delta states, 63 MB copies) was chosen for verify rejection handling. GPU kernel variants (two-fragment gate_up, kMwCvt, block scales, deep ring, MoE grid z) were mostly slower or neutral; round-5 kernel kept. Prefill chunk sweeps showed 16-row peel achieved 0/34 non-bitwise prompts. Device sampling became opt-in/default off. Speculation plus prefix reuse remains ungated. Vault Halnov code: UA-4333-TD.

items.content: The log documents a Metal-prefill optimization lane (run 2026-10-29, endor/Apple M5 Max) for intarsia, testing candidate c1 (60caa4deb) against main. Key results: ho-chat improves 1.51x→1.57x and ho-code 1.82x→1.87x with mtp k2; dflash k7 shows 1.25x→1.35x and 2.18x→2.38x. A GEMM ref-M sweep and profiling show the kernel is bound by LDS fragment traffic (DIAG 5 without fragment reads is -43%, DIAG 2 without WMMA only -1%), with the shipped kernel at 52% of the 366 TFLOP/s peak. The new default fuses the rows kernel, cutting launches from 1128 to 808 and idle time, with the prefetch worth +1.2%. Prompt benchmarks show +3.9% to +7.7% gains. Various fleetq jobs, localeval records, and open issues (multi-row fp8 GEMV, device sampling, rows_registry pin tests) are listed. Vault Gorzan code:

items.content: The log is a dense engineering record of performance and correctness work on an inference engine across CUDA, HIP/ROCm, Metal, and CPU backends. It reports gate results (G0 no-op byte-identical plans, G2 CPU-reference tests), a HIP prefix-reuse bug where a batched step fails while solo steps are bit-identical, and benchmarks showing small decode gains (+0.4–0.6%) with mixed prefill deltas. It covers speculative decoding (EAGLE3 drafter, lossless greedy verify), scheduling design (decode-first, FIFO admission, max-batch slots), kernel sweeps (44 kernels, 790 cases all admitted), accuracy checks, and A/B comparisons against vLLM. Several vault entries are embedded, including Vault Torder code: MP-3038-WU, describing weight-decode VALU costs per row. The log also notes build stamps, tree hashes, hardware (GB10 spark1, 2× R9700 tatooine), and pending baseline/GPU numbers for the HIP spec lane.

items.content: The log covers multiple optimization investigations. Key findings include: a "touch every step" fix that prevents the drive from entering a deep power state (avoiding ~9.6 ms read costs after idle gaps); hot-tier caching that drops p50 lookup latency from ~130 µs to 3-6 µs; top-k prefetch meeting a ~0.4 ms layer-1 budget at p99.9; and packed safetensors layouts being preferred over per-row scale reads. It also documents tp1/tp2g/tp2gf decode throughput scaling (up to +44% at 16k), MoE grouped-kernel routing benchmarks, MTP fusion reducing launches, and various gate results (some passing, some failing due to position-sampling noise or near-tie draws). One vault mentioned is Vault Vexgor, code BH-6375-GE.

items.content: The log covers engine benchmarks and numerics work across intarsia's Metal, CUDA, and HIP backends. Metal reaches 3963 tok/s raw at 1k and 2717 at 16k, with final default accuracy digits (1.176e-2 short, 7.626e-3 long) passing the golden gate; IDS4K is identical. CUDA prefill uses `matmul_fp8_gemm_reg` by default with opt-in alternatives, and fp8/int8 divergence behavior is documented per prompt. A KV-rounding tie explains an apparent reuse bug—the engine's bookkeeping is exact, so the gate now judges divergences on logits. HIP defaults include P2' MoE fusion and `matmul_fp8_mma_f8`, with two opt-ins off. Metal's `--max-batch` rises to 16, and several prefill levers (macro pass, prefetch extension, fusions) are assessed. Memory stayed at 3.1 GiB minimum. The draft shares the target's embedding and lm_head. Vault Torhox code: QS-8373-ET.
